ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the river starts from point A on the left and flows to the right. At the first split, there is a downward branch labeled 1/3 beside it, and the other branch continues to flow to the right. The branch continuing to the right splits a second time on the right side; in the second split, the lower branch is labeled 3/4 beside it, and the upper branch leads to point B. Then reason: In the first split, the downward branch takes away 1/3 of the original water, so the second branch continuing to the right has 1 - 1/3 = 2/3 left. In the second split, the lower branch takes away 3/4 of this branch, so the upper branch leading to B takes the remaining 1 - 3/4 = 1/4. Therefore the proportion of the original water that flows to B is 2/3 × 1/4 = 2/12 = 1/6.
